correctness.rationale: Poisson thinning gives independent site failures e^{-a x_1}, e^{-a x_2}, e^{-b x_3}. At fixed weak-site allocation, the product of high-site failures is fixed and their sum is uniquely minimized by equal efforts (AM-GM). The remaining scalar failure probability is \(u^2+2u(1-u)v\), with derivative \(u[u(1-v)+(1-2h)v(1-u)]\). For \(h\le1/2\) the unique minimizer is \(z=0\); for \(h>1/2\) the derivative changes sign exactly once because (exp(hz)-1)/(exp((B-z)/2)-1) increases strictly from zero to infinity. Logarithmic root asymptotics establish both stated limits. The standalone checker was replayed and passed 18898 supplementary assertions; these are not substitutes for the continuum proof. All parameter boundaries, equality cases, and model assumptions are stated.

value.rationale: Reintroduction programs naturally seek at least two independently established habitats rather than a single founder site; this is the smallest nontrivial redundancy objective. The exact \(b/a=1/2\) cutoff identifies when a lower-efficiency third habitat must receive no introduction budget or must receive positive effort, for all budgets. The unique optimizer and small-/large-budget fractions quantify a substantial shift in the optimal weak-site share. The result is a nontrivial full parameter classification, not a mere fixed-parameter evaluation; however biological applicability requires independent Poisson success and is expressly not a persistence result.
